notes: Follow-up to 13882 (Tong quan/Bao cao/Nhat ky loi single-source workflow summary). dueSoon ('Sap qua han') was computed with a hardcoded 3-calendar-day window inside classifyViolationWorkflowStatus() - not tied to the real response-deadline policy, so it would silently drift if Admin changes the configured response window. Fixed: exported operationTimingPolicy() from lib/checklist-tasks.js (no behavior change to that function); classifyViolationWorkflowStatus() now takes an optional timingPolicy argument and derives the dueSoon window from it - employeeResponseDays while waiting on the employee, reviewerResponseDays while in explanation/waiting on Admin - falling back to 3 days ONLY when the policy setting is genuinely unreadable (same fallback convention as boundedDays() in checklist-tasks.js). getChecklistViolationWorkflowSummary() (lib/checklist-reports.js) and listChecklistViolations()'s due_soon drill-down filter (lib/checklist-violations.js) both fetch operationTimingPolicy() once per request and pass it into every classify call - no per-record extra query. Added a regression case to scripts/test-checklist-violation-workflow-summary.js that sets employeeResponseDays=5/reviewerResponseDays=1 and proves dueSoon follows the configured values (would fail under the old hardcoded 3-day logic). Pre-release hardening: added scripts/test-checklist-violation-permission-scope.js, a multi-department/multi-branch/multi-employee permission-scope regression covering Admin, Tro ly GD, Truong bo phan, Truong ca (viewScope wider than reviewScope - the case that used to diverge), Quan ly truc tiep (view-only), Chi xem bao cao (no view_violations) and Nhan vien; it runs a real in-memory filtering query engine (not canned per-table responses) so out-of-scope fixture rows would actually leak through if a scope filter were ever dropped, and cross-checks every summary bucket against listChecklistViolations({workflowStatus}) for the same actor/scope. No permission preset changed, no new API added, no workflowStatus bucket key redefined.
